source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); Schedule S line A14 (ip25 PDF page 21), instructions PDF page 12 'Retirement benefits specifically exempt from Kansas Income Tax' (the list names federal, railroad and Kansas plans only); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = federal public pension (you) 30,000.00 + Missouri public pension (spouse) 30,000.00 + interest 5,000.00 = 65,000.00. Federal taxable income = 65,000.00 - standard deduction 33,100.00 (31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 31,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). Schedule S Part A: line A1 0.00; lines A2-A8 0.00; line A9 total additions 0.00. Line A10 0.00; lines A11-A13 0.00; line A14 retirement benefits specifically exempt: federal retirement benefits (you) 30,000.00 = 30,000.00; lines A15-A25 0.00; line A26 total subtractions = 30,000.00; line A27 net modification = 0.00 - 30,000.00 = -30,000.00. Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 65,000.00; line 2 modifications -30,000.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 65,000.00 + (-30,000.00) = 35,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (married filing joint), worksheet for people 65 or older: 1 box checked (you), 8,240.00 + 1 x 700.00 = 8,940.00 (the worksheet prints 8,940.00); line 5 exemption allowance (2 exemptions) 18,320.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 8,940.00 + 18,320.00 = 27,260.00; line 7 taxable income = 35,000.00 - 27,260.00 = 7,740.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 7,740.00 = 402.4800 = 402.48. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 7,701-7,750, married filing joint column, PDF page 27, gives 402; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 402.48. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 402.48. Two public pensions of the same size: the federal one comes off, the Missouri one stays, as another state's plan is not on line A14.
accepted_approximations: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
